issue: BHI computation uses a single conditionRating value replicated across all 4 element slots (Deck, Substructure, Superstructure, Approach all receive the same scalar). AP-G71.8 and AS 5100-7 require BHI = SUM(element_weight x actual_element_condition_score) / SUM(element_weight) using distinct per-element ratings from BridgeInspectionElements. Using one scalar makes the formula meaningless and collapses to conditionRating x constant.
fix: Query BridgeInspectionElements for the bridge's latest inspection and map SIMS element codes to AP-G71.8 weights (deck 25%, substructure 30%, superstructure 30%, approach 15%). Fall back to single-rating proxy only when no element records exist and log a data-quality flag.

issue: Two incompatible BHI engines coexist: srv/lib/bhi-calculator.js (v2.1, element scores 1-5, output 20-100, 5 elements: superstructure/substructure/deck/bearing/joint, peer-review ref ADR-BHI-001 noted but unsigned) and srv/bhi-bsi-engine.js (multi-modal, scores 1-10, output 0-100, variable elements). The test suite tests lib/bhi-calculator.js but admin-service.js uses bhi-bsi-engine.js in production. No test exists for bhi-bsi-engine.js. The two engines produce different results for the same bridge.
fix: Designate lib/bhi-calculator.js (v2.1, AS 5100-7 aligned, tested) as the production engine. Replace computeBhiBsi calls in admin-service.js with calculateBHI. Retire bhi-bsi-engine.js or clearly label it experimental. Write a test for the chosen engine using actual AP-G71.8 specimen calculations to verify against published reference results.

issue: Two incompatible BSI formulas coexist. admin-service.js lines 427-440 implements: BSI = structural(conditionRating/10 x 55) + width(bsiWidthRating/10 x 15) + barrier(constant 5/10 x 15) + route(constant 5/10 x 15). Barrier and route default to constant 5 regardless of actual data, capping the achievable maximum at 85 rather than 100. srv/lib/bsi-calculator.js implements the documented FHWA-adapted formula: BSI = (structuralAdequacy x 0.55) + (serviceability x 0.30) + (essentiality x 0.15). The two implementations diverge significantly for real bridge data.
fix: Unify on srv/lib/bsi-calculator.js. Update admin-service.js after('READ', Bridges) to call calculateBSI() with real inputs: bhiScore from element ratings, loadRatingFactor from BridgeCapacities, serviceability inputs (deckCondition, geometricAlignment, verticalClearance, approachCondition), and essentiality inputs (aadt, detourLengthKm, freightRoute flags).

issue: conditionRating uses a 1-10 scale (@assert.range:[1,10]) that is not documented in any Australian bridge management standard. AS 5100-7 and SIMS define the condition grade scale as 1-5 (1=As New, 5=Very Poor). The legacy nhvr.Bridge entity correctly uses a 1-5 scale (conditionRatingTfnsw). BridgeInspectionElements.currentConditionRating also uses 1-5 (@assert.range:[1,5]) making the two scales inconsistent. In admin-service.js line 454-459, the 1-10 conditionRating value is passed directly as a 1-5 element rating to the BHI engine, producing systematically inflated BHI scores.
fix: Standardise on the AS 5100-7 1-5 scale. Add conditionRatingExtended:Integer @assert.range:[1,10] for backward compatibility if needed. Annotate conditionRating with @Common.QuickInfo documenting the scale and its relationship to TfNSW/SIMS ratings. Fix the BHI computation to convert scale before passing to element ratings.

issue: ISO 55000 asset classification gaps: (1) assetClass:String(40) is free-text with no FK to AssetClasses lookup — unenforced classification. (2) No assetType sub-classification field (e.g. Road Bridge | Rail Bridge | Pedestrian | Culvert). (3) No ISO 55000 criticality field based on consequence-of-failure analysis — importanceLevel is an NHVR field meaning network importance, not failure criticality. (4) lifecycleStage:String(30) in extensions.cds has no enum validation and no AMAF-aligned values.
fix: (1) Add FK association assetClassRef to AssetClasses. (2) Add assetType:String(40) with AssetTypes lookup. (3) Add criticalityISO:String(20) enum (Critical|High|Medium|Low) derived from consequence-of-failure analysis. (4) Convert lifecycleStage to a CDS enum type with AMAF-aligned values: Planning|Design|Construction|Commissioning|Operation|Maintenance|Rehabilitation|Decommissioning.

issue: ISO 55000 Whole-of-Life Cost (WoLC) gaps: (1) No currentReplacementCost (CRC) field separate from replacementCostEstimate — CRC is the insurance/replacement value used in financial reporting. (2) No writtenDownValue (WDV) field needed for the financial-proxy BHI in srv/lib/bhi-calculator.js line 81 which references WDV but this field does not exist in any schema entity. (3) No whole-of-life NPV fields (discount rate, depreciation method). (4) remainingEconomicLifeYears exists only on LoadRatingCertificates (load-ratings.cds line 41) not at asset level.
fix: Add to bridge-entity.cds or extensions.cds: currentReplacementCost:Decimal(14,2), writtenDownValue:Decimal(14,2), remainingEconomicLifeYears:Integer, depreciationMethod:String(20), lccReference:String(40). This makes calculateBHIFromFinancials() in bhi-calculator.js callable with real persisted data.

issue: BridgeDefects.defectCode:String(20) is a free-text field with no FK to the DefectCodes CodeList entity (db/schema.cds line 311). There is no validation that defectCode matches an entry in DefectCodes. AustRoads bridge defect catalogue and SIMS require standardised defect codes — a bridge record can have defectCode='XYZ123' that does not exist in DefectCodes without any error.
fix: Add defectCodeRef:Association to DefectCodes on defectCodeRef.code = defectCode or change defectCode to a direct FK. Populate the DefectCodes seed CSV with the standard AustRoads/SIMS defect code catalogue. Add server-side validation in the defects handler to reject unknown codes. Annotate with @Common.ValueList pointing to DefectCodes.

issue: Scale mismatch between inspection entities: BridgeInspections.overallConditionRating uses 1-10 scale (line 38: @assert.range:[1,10]) but BridgeInspectionElements.currentConditionRating uses AS 5100-7 1-5 scale (elements.cds line 20). lib/bhi-calculator.js expects 1-5 input. In admin-service.js line 454-459, the 1-10 overallConditionRating value is passed directly as a 1-5 element score — a conditionRating=5 (mid-range on 1-10) is treated as maximum (5 of 5), producing BHI=100 instead of the correct ~50.
fix: Normalise the scale before passing to BHI engine: convert 1-10 rating to 1-5 by ceil(conditionRating/2) or by explicit mapping. Alternatively standardise BridgeInspections.overallConditionRating to use @assert.range:[1,5] matching BridgeInspectionElements. Document chosen scale with @Common.QuickInfo on both entities.

issue: Spatial columns are Decimal(15,6) lat/lon free fields without HANA native ST_Point/ST_Geometry types. Consequences: (1) No SRID enforcement at DB level — coordinateDatum:String(20) in extensions.cds is a free-text string not a type-enforced SRID 7844 (GDA2020). (2) No HANA spatial indexes — proximity queries use application-code haversine which is slow at scale. (3) No ST_WithinDistance, ST_Buffer, or ST_Contains operations available without extracting to separate HANA spatial columns. Australian spatial data regulations require GDA2020 (SRID 7844).
fix: Add geoPoint field using HANA ST_Point type with SRID 7844. Populate it via a before('SAVE') handler from latitude/longitude. Update srv/reports-api.js and map/api to use ST_WithinDistance for proximity queries. Add DB-level check constraint that SRID = 7844.

issue: LRS (Linear Referencing System) fields are fragmented and inconsistently named: extensions.cds has roadId:String(20), startSlk:Decimal(10,3), endSlk:Decimal(10,3) (undocumented km units) without lrs_offset_from/lrs_offset_to naming per ISO 19148. BridgeCarriageways (gap-entities.cds) has distanceFromStartKm but no roadId FK. nhvr.Bridge has no LRS fields at all. There is no Route association on bridge.management.Bridges (only on nhvr.Bridge). LRS data is scattered across three entities with different naming conventions and no cross-reference.
fix: Standardise LRS: rename startSlk to lrsOffsetFromKm and endSlk to lrsOffsetToKm with unit annotation. Add lrsNetworkCode:String(20) (RINR/RIND per TfNSW SDAM). Link BridgeCarriageways.roadId as FK to a RoadNetwork lookup. Add @Common.QuickInfo:'Chainage in km per TfNSW SDAM LRS' on all LRS fields.

issue: No asset hierarchy (parent FK or self-association) on bridge.management.Bridges. ISO 55000 S6.4 requires an asset hierarchy for portfolio management. AGAM S3.1 requires asset-parent-child relationships for multi-structure complexes. BridgeElements has parentElement self-association but the primary asset entity does not, making it impossible to model a bridge complex (e.g. a multi-structure interchange where one parent bridges groups multiple child structures).
fix: Add parentBridge:Association to Bridges (nullable self-referencing FK) and back-association children:Association to many Bridges on children.parentBridge = $self. Follow the pattern already established by the Restrictions entity's parent/children self-associations in db/schema.cds lines 114-116.

issue: scoreToLevel() maps risk score to level using scalar thresholds only. TfNSW TS01501 S4.3 requires a consequence-caps rule: when consequence=5 (Catastrophic) and likelihood>=3, the risk level must be Extreme regardless of the product score. The current code at line 116-121 returns High for score 10-14. Score=15 (likelihood=3 x consequence=5) correctly returns Extreme. But score=12 (likelihood=3 x consequence=4 — Major consequence) returns High when TfNSW TS01501 Table 1 classifies this cell as Extreme (red). The scalar product alone is insufficient for the 5x5 colour matrix.
fix: After computing inherentRiskLevel from scoreToLevel(), apply consequence override: if (consequence >= 5 && likelihood >= 3) set 'Extreme'. If (consequence >= 4 && likelihood >= 4) set 'Extreme'. Implement the full TfNSW TS01501 Table 1 colour matrix as a lookup object rather than threshold comparison. Apply same logic to residual risk level computation.

issue: BridgeInspections.inspector:String(111) is free-text with no FK to a personnel/accreditation registry. inspectorAccreditationNumber:String(40) is also free-text (line 22). TfNSW-BIM S3.1 requires Principal and Detailed inspection types to be performed by Austroads-accredited inspectors with verified NER (National Engineering Register) numbers. qualificationExpiry:Date (line 24) exists but there is no server-side check that qualificationExpiry >= inspectionDate. Any string can be entered as inspector name with no verification.
fix: Add inspectorUserId:String(111) as a reference to the CAP user ID (req.user.id). Add server-side validation: when inspectionType is Principal or Detailed, check qualificationExpiry >= inspectionDate and return req.error(422) if expired. Consider an InspectorAccreditation lookup entity storing NER numbers, accreditation levels, and expiry dates.

issue: BridgeMaintenanceActions has no s4OrderId or s4NotificationId fields — no work order or notification reference for SAP PM integration. BridgeInspections has s4InspectionOrderRef and s4NotificationRef (defects.cds lines 33-34) and BridgeDefects has s4NotificationId (line 93) but no s4OrderId for repair work orders. No Measuring Document (MeasDoc) pattern exists — there is no MeasuringPoint or structured condition measurement history entity for SAP PM integration.
fix: Add to BridgeMaintenanceActions: s4NotificationId:String(12), s4OrderId:String(12), s4OrderType:String(4) (PM01|PM02|PM03). Add MeasuringPoint concept: BridgeMeasuringPoints entity with measurementCode and description, and BridgeMeasurements entity for reading history (readingValue, unit, readingDate, inspector). This enables SSAM-compliant SAP PM MeasDoc integration.

issue: BridgeScourAssessments.scourRisk:String(20) is a free-text field. AP-G71.8 S5.1 requires the 5-level numeric scour risk score (1-5: VeryLow/Low/Medium/High/VeryHigh) on the primary assessment record. The ap71ScoreNumeric:Integer @assert.range:[1,5] exists only on BridgeScourAssessmentDetail (nhvr-compliance.cds line 59) — a hydraulic sub-record, not the primary assessment. BridgeScourAssessments also lacks hydraulicModelRef and hydraulicModelType (only on the Detail entity). AP-G71.8 S3.2 requires hydraulic model reference on the primary assessment.
fix: Add to BridgeScourAssessments: ap71ScoreNumeric:Integer @assert.range:[1,5], scourRiskCategoryAp71:String(20) (VeryLow|Low|Medium|High|VeryHigh), hydraulicModelRequired:Boolean default false. Synchronise bridge.management.Bridges.scourRisk from BridgeScourAssessments.scourRiskCategoryAp71 via the same sync pattern used for conditionRating.

issue: BridgeDefects.severity:Integer @assert.range:[1,4] scale direction is not documented in the schema. CLAUDE.md says 1=Low, 4=Critical (ascending severity) which matches TfNSW-BIM S4.2. AGAM uses the inverse (1=Critical, 4=Low). The urgency field (line 76) has the same 1-4 range with no documented meaning. Without enum type documentation, a new developer can implement logic using the wrong direction, causing critical defects to be treated as minor (as previously occurred per CLAUDE.md).
fix: Convert severity and urgency to CDS enum types: type DefectSeverity : Integer enum { Minor=1; Moderate=2; Significant=3; Critical=4 } aligning with TfNSW-BIM S4.2. type DefectUrgency : Integer enum { Low=1; Medium=2; High=3; Immediate=4 }. Add @Common.QuickInfo annotations. This self-documents the scale direction in the schema and prevents future inversion bugs.

issue: inspectionFrequencyYears:Integer (line 69) is a manually-entered static field. AGAM S4.2 requires inspection frequency to be risk-derived — bridges with lower condition ratings or higher risk scores must trigger shorter inspection intervals. nextInspectionDue:Date (line 71) is not auto-computed from lastInspectionDate + inspectionFrequencyYears. No handler auto-calculates nextInspectionDue when an inspection is completed (only conditionRating/nhvrAssessed are synced per CLAUDE.md). nhvr.Bridge also has inspectionFrequencyYears:Integer default 2 as a static default.
fix: Add auto-computation of nextInspectionDue in admin-service.js after inspection completion: nextInspectionDue = lastInspectionDate + inspectionFrequencyYears years. Add an InspectionFrequencyRules entity mapping conditionRating ranges to required frequency (e.g. rating 1-3: 1yr, 4-6: 2yr, 7-10: 5yr per TfNSW-BIM S3.5). Auto-set inspectionFrequencyYears from the rule table when a new inspection is completed.

issue: NhvrRouteAssessments.approvedVehicleClasses:LargeString (line 19) stores approved classes as free text while NhvrApprovedVehicleClasses composition child entity (line 74) stores the same data in structured form (per-class maxGrossMass and conditions). Two representations of the same data create consistency risk. HVNL SS154-157 requires per-vehicle-class approval records with explicit mass limits. The LargeString field is redundant and may diverge from the structured sub-table.
fix: Remove NhvrRouteAssessments.approvedVehicleClasses:LargeString. All vehicle class approvals must go through the NhvrApprovedVehicleClasses composition child. Update the UI to create/edit child records. Add a migration script to parse existing LargeString JSON into NhvrApprovedVehicleClasses records.

issue: Two overlapping boolean lifecycle flags: isActive:Boolean default true (line 87) and isDeleted:Boolean default false (line 88). These allow inconsistent states (isActive=true AND isDeleted=true). ISO 55000 requires a defined lifecycle state machine. nhvr.Bridge (core.cds) has the same two-boolean anti-pattern. No handler enforces mutual consistency between the two flags or prevents contradictory states.
fix: Replace two-boolean pattern with assetLifecycleStatus:String(20) enum: Active|Decommissioned|Demolished|Archived|Draft. Add virtual isActive computed as assetLifecycleStatus === 'Active' for backwards compatibility. Migrate existing data: isActive=true/isDeleted=false -> 'Active', isActive=false/isDeleted=false -> 'Decommissioned', isActive=false/isDeleted=true -> 'Archived'.

issue: BridgeInspections.inspectionType:String(40) @mandatory is free-text with no association to the InspectionTypes CodeList entity (db/schema.cds line 385). Same issue on Bridges.inspectionType (bridge-entity.cds line 69). AS 5100-7 S3.2 defines four standard inspection types. Free-text allows non-standard values that cannot be filtered or reported reliably, and list reports cannot group inspections by type.
fix: Change BridgeInspections.inspectionType to FK association to InspectionTypes code lookup. Populate InspectionTypes seed CSV with ROUTINE_VISUAL, DETAILED, PRINCIPAL, SPECIAL_SCOUR, UNDERWATER, LOAD_RATING per AS 5100-7 S3.2. Apply same FK on Bridges.inspectionType. Add @Common.ValueList annotation for FE4 value-help dropdown.

issue: BridgeElements.s4EquipmentNumber:String(18) (line 38) has no s4SyncStatus field. BridgeDefects has s4SyncStatus (defects.cds line 95) and Bridges has s4EamSyncStatus (extensions.cds line 48) but BridgeElements and BridgeMehComponents (gap-entities.cds line 73) lack sync status tracking. Without a sync status field, it is impossible to determine which elements have been synchronised to SAP PM Equipment master records.
fix: Add s4SyncStatus:String(20) default 'NOT_LINKED' and s4SyncedAt:Timestamp to both BridgeElements and BridgeMehComponents. This makes EAM sync status consistent across all entities carrying s4EquipmentNumber and enables the EAM integration dashboard to report coverage percentage.

issue: LoadRatingCertificates.dynamicLoadAllowance defaults to 1.4 (line 33). AS 5100.7:2017 Table 6.2 specifies DLA values that vary by span length: 0.40 for spans <=33m, 0.30 for 33-100m, 0.20 for >100m. The value 1.4 appears to be (1 + 0.40) — the full dynamic factor — rather than just the DLA add-on. If this value is used in rating calculations without engineer override, it will systematically overestimate dynamic loading for long-span bridges.
fix: Change default to null. Add @Common.QuickInfo: 'DLA per AS 5100.7 Table 6.2: 0.40 (<=33m span), 0.30 (33-100m), 0.20 (>100m). Enter the DLA factor not (1+DLA).' Add a suggested-value computation in the handler based on bridge spanLength. Remove the 1.4 default to prevent incorrect defaults propagating into rating calculations.

issue: residualRiskScore and residualRiskLevel are not auto-computed when residualLikelihood and residualConsequence are entered. Only inherentRiskScore is auto-computed (lines 24-37). ISO 31000 S6.6 requires residual risk to be computed as residualLikelihood x residualConsequence with level derived from the same matrix. If both residual fields are entered but residualRiskScore is left null, the risk register is silently incomplete.
fix: Extend before(['CREATE','UPDATE'], 'BridgeRiskAssessments') to also compute residualRiskScore = residualLikelihood x residualConsequence and residualRiskLevel = scoreToLevel(residualRiskScore) when both residual input fields are non-null. Apply the same partial-UPDATE logic already used for inherent risk (fetch existing values, merge, compute). Apply consequence-caps override consistently to both inherent and residual risk levels.

issue: importanceLevel:Integer @assert.range:[1,4] encoding (1=Critical, 4=Ordinary) is inverted relative to AS 5100.1 S B4 which defines Importance Level as IL1=low consequence to IL4=high consequence (ascending severity). nhvr.Bridge.importanceLevel (core.cds line 71) is String(20) with values Critical|Essential|Important|Ordinary — incompatible type. The BHI engine importanceFactor in bhi-bsi-engine.js line 29 uses: importanceFactor = 0.85 + (ic-1) x 0.03, where ic=1 gives the lowest factor — this correctly treats 1 as least important. However the BMS entity documentation says 1=Critical (most important). The direction of the importance factor effect is therefore inverted from the AS 5100.1 standard.
fix: Standardise to AS 5100.1 IL1-IL4 ascending encoding (IL1=low/ordinary, IL4=critical/high). Update importanceFactor in bhi-bsi-engine.js to use: importanceFactor = 0.85 + (ic-1) x 0.03 where ic=IL4=4 gives highest factor (0.94) for most important. Align nhvr.Bridge.importanceLevel to the same Integer encoding. Add @Common.QuickInfo documenting AS 5100.1 IL1-IL4.

issue: BridgeInspectionElements.elementType:String(50) is free-text (no simsElementCode field) unlike BridgeElements which has simsElementCode:String(20) (elements.cds line 10). SIMS requires condition states CS1-CS4 to be recorded against standardised SIMS element codes (DEK/ABT/PRM/BRG/EXP/DRN/GRD/FON/PRA). Without a simsElementCode on inspection element records, condition state data cannot be aggregated across inspections for element-level trending or benchmarked against national SIMS standards.
fix: Add simsElementCode:String(20) to BridgeInspectionElements. Add elementRef:Association to BridgeElements to optionally link the inspection element record to the structured element register. Change elementType to use an enum type or Association to a SIMS element type lookup table.

issue: averageDailyTraffic:Integer (line 51) has no aadtSurveyDate field. AADT changes over time and must carry a survey date for lifecycle cost and risk calculations. nhvr.Bridge has aadtLastRecordedDate:Date (core.cds line 107) but bridge.management.Bridges does not. The AssetIQ scoring engine uses heavyVehiclePercent (admin-service.js line 1599) without validating data currency. Stale traffic data (e.g. 10-year-old counts) silently produce incorrect traffic factor scores.
fix: Add aadtSurveyDate:Date and heavyVehicleSurveyDate:Date to bridge-entity.cds. In the AssetIQ scoring handler, add a staleness check: if aadtSurveyDate is more than 5 years ago, apply a data-quality flag and reduce confidence in the traffic factor. Mirror the nhvr.Bridge pattern (aadtLastRecordedDate).

issue: LoadRatingCertificates.ratingBasis:String(40) (line 53, values 'Austroads Guide | AS 5100 | Load Testing | Proof Loading') overlaps semantically with the LoadRatingMethod enum (enum-types.cds line 10: AS5100, NAASRA, LoadTesting). Two different fields represent the same concept across two entities (BridgeLoadRatings and LoadRatingCertificates) with inconsistent terminology. Proof Loading does not appear in LoadRatingMethod.
fix: Add ProofLoading to the LoadRatingMethod enum in enum-types.cds. Replace LoadRatingCertificates.ratingBasis:String(40) with ratingBasis:LoadRatingMethod to reuse the same enum. This eliminates the semantic duplicate and ensures consistent terminology across both rating entities.

issue: clearanceHeight:Decimal(9,2) (line 24) has no annotation indicating whether it is surveyed or posted clearance. AS 1742.2 distinguishes between physical surveyed clearance and legal posted clearance (the restriction sign value). extensions.cds adds clearanceHeightSurveyed and clearanceHeightPosted (lines 63-64) but the base clearanceHeight field is ambiguous. Three clearance fields exist with no documented semantic relationship.
fix: Annotate clearanceHeight with @Common.QuickInfo: 'Legal posted clearance per AS 1742.2. Surveyed physical measurement is in clearanceHeightSurveyed field.' Consider deprecating clearanceHeight in favour of the two explicit fields and computing clearanceHeight as virtual = clearanceHeightPosted for backwards compatibility.

issue: BridgeMaintenanceActions.MaintenanceActionType enum (Repair, Preventive, Emergency, Inspection, Rehabilitation, Replacement) does not map to SAP PM notification types (M1 Malfunction Report, M2 Activity Report) or SAP PM order categories (PM01 corrective, PM02 preventive, PM03 inspection, PM04 refurbishment). Without this mapping, data exchange with SAP PM requires manual re-classification.
fix: Add s4NotificationType:String(4) (M1|M2|M3) and s4OrderType:String(4) (PM01|PM02|PM03|PM04) to BridgeMaintenanceActions. Add a handler computation: actionType=Emergency -> PM01/M1, Preventive -> PM02/M2, Inspection -> PM03/M2. Document the mapping in a SystemConfig entry or in a code comment as an ADR.

issue: InspectionStandard enum includes NAASRA='NAASRA 1992' (line 18). The NAASRA 1992 bridge inspection standard was superseded by AS 5100-7. Including it in the active enum without a deprecated indicator may lead inspectors to select it for new inspections. AGAM enum value is 'AGAM:2013' but the current edition is AGAM 2021. Both references are outdated.
fix: Rename AGAM value to 'AGAM:2021'. Add a UI-side warning (not block) when NAASRA is selected: 'NAASRA 1992 is superseded by AS 5100-7. Please confirm.' Alternatively add a DeprecatedStandards lookup that marks NAASRA as withdrawn and triggers a validation warning in the inspection handler.
